title: Systematic modulation of superconducting gap dynamics in YBCO|BNT|YBCO Josephson Junctions through THz field interaction and BNT ferroelectric barrier
authors: Sukhanidhan Singh, Muthukkumaran Karthikeyan, Geoffrey Chanda, Thanayut Kaewmaraya, Pairot Moontragoon, Guoxing Sun, Zongjin Li, Anucha Watcharapasorn
abstract: The integration of ferroelectric barriers into high-temperature Josephson junctions offers a pathway to tunable superconducting quantum devices. Here, we demonstrate robust Josephson coupling in YBa2Cu3O7-x (YBCO)/Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3 (BNT)/YBCO trilayer junctions incorporating a 40 nm ferroelectric BNT barrier. Epitaxial trilayers were fabricated by pulsed laser deposition on SrTiO3 substrates and investigated under broadband terahertz (THz) irradiation (0.5-2.5 THz). At 1.5 THz, close to the Josephson plasma resonance, the BNT polarization increased from 33.4 to 46.4 uC/cm2 at 30 K, enhancing superconducting transport. The junctions exhibited a well-defined zero-voltage supercurrent branch, with the critical current Ic(T) remaining nearly constant up to 60 K and reaching 468.2 uA under 1.5 THz excitation, evidencing strong phase coherence. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy revealed an enhanced superconducting gap in YBCO/BNT/YBCO (Delta = 1.3 meV) compared with pure YBCO (Delta = 1.05 meV), while optical conductivity measurements showed a reduction in conductivity and gap with increasing temperature, consistent with BCS theory under THz excitation. Atomic force microscopy and X-ray reflectivity confirmed uniform morphology and sharp interfaces, excluding defect-mediated transport. Magnetic field modulation of Ic(B) exhibited a canonical Fraunhofer interference pattern, and resistance mapping revealed alternating lobes of high and low dissipation, indicating coherent Josephson tunneling. These results establish that Josephson coupling is intrinsic to the YBCO/BNT/YBCO junctions, enabled by the dipolar character and dynamic THz response of the BNT barrier. This study identifies BNT as a viable, tunable barrier material for next-generation high-Tc superconducting quantum devices.
summary: This research demonstrates that ferroelectric BNT barriers can be used to create Josephson junctions whose superconducting properties are dynamically controlled by external Terahertz (THz) radiation. By coupling THz fields to the BNT polarization, researchers successfully modulated both the critical current and the superconducting energy gap in YBCO/BNT/YBCO structures. This establishes a pathway for building next-generation, light-controlled superconducting quantum devices.
main_problem: The study aims to systematically modulate superconducting gap dynamics in YBCO|BNT|YBCO Josephson Junctions by utilizing the interaction between external Terahertz (THz) fields and the ferroelectric polarization of the BNT barrier.
main_result: The research demonstrates that THz irradiation can dynamically enhance the critical current ($I_c$) and increase the superconducting gap ($\Delta$), confirming that the Josephson coupling is intrinsically controlled by the tunable, dipolar response of the ferroelectric BNT barrier.
method: A combination of epitaxial thin-film deposition (PLD) to create high-quality trilayers, electrical transport measurements ($I$-$V$, $dI/dV$) under THz excitation, and theoretical modeling using a modified Josephson junction Hamiltonian was employed.
model_or_system: The physical system is the YBCO|BNT|YBCO Josephson Junction. The dynamics are modeled by incorporating a time-dependent modulation term ($\mathcal{H}_{mod}$) into the standard Josephson Hamiltonian, where this modulation arises from the THz-induced polarization ($P_{THz}(t)$) within the BNT ferroelectric barrier.
key_observables: Superconducting gap ($\Delta$), critical current ($I_c$) under THz excitation, BNT polarization ($P$), and Fraunhofer interference patterns in $I_c(B)$.
important_parameters: THz frequency (0.5-2.5 THz), ferroelectric polarization magnitude ($33.4 	o 46.4 \mu	ext{C}/	ext{cm}^2$), and superconducting gap values ($\Delta = 1.3 	ext{ meV}$ vs $1.05 	ext{ meV}$).
main_assumptions: The coupling mechanism is assumed to be dominated by the dipolar interaction between the THz field/polarization and the junction capacitance, leading to a time-dependent barrier potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural characterization (XRD/XRR) confirming high epitaxial quality; energy diagrams show how the external THz field introduces an additional gap ($E_g$) into the Josephson coupling energy ($	ext{E}_{	ext{J}}$); and spectroscopic plots detail the modulation of $\Delta$ and $I_c$.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from system definition (YBCO/BNT/YBCO stack) to theoretical modeling incorporating THz interaction, followed by detailed experimental characterization (structural confirmation via XRR/XRD, electrical measurements under THz), culminating in the demonstration of dynamic control over superconducting parameters.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges condensed matter physics (superconductivity, high-Tc cuprates) with quantum optics and materials science (ferroelectrics, THz response). The ability to use an external electromagnetic field to tune a fundamental quantum parameter like the superconducting gap is highly relevant for developing tunable quantum devices.
